subject: Is R-INLA able to handle the nested error component estimation?

messages.author: e9ab831d77228443
messages.subject: Is R-INLA able to handle the nested error component estimation?
parts:
Hi everyone

I am a green hand of applying R-INLA. It seems that INLA is very helpful to handle latent Gaussian models (GLMM, HLM, GAMM, etc.). 
I have a unbalanced spatio-temporal panel data set.  The relevant modeling is to apply a nested error component regression model.  

EX:

y_{ijt}=x_{ijt}+u_{ijt}      i=1,..,M ; j=1,..,N ; t=1,...T
where y_{ijt} could denote the output of the j th firm in the i th industry for the tt h time period. x_{ijt} denotes a vector of k non-stochastic inputs. 

The disturbance is given by
u_{ijt}=\mu _{i}+v_{ij}+\varepsilon _{ijt}     i=1,..,M ; j=1,..,N ; t=1,...T

where \mu _{i} denotes the i th un-observable industry specific effect which is assumed to be i.i.d. (0, \sigma _{\mu }^{2} ), v_{ij} denotes the nested effect of the j th firm within the i th industry which is assumed to be i.i.d. (0, \sigma _{v }^{2} ) and 
\varepsilon _{ijt} denotes the remainder disturbance which is also assumed to be i.i.d. (0, \sigma _{\varepsilon  }^{2} ). The \mu _{i} v_{ij} and \varepsilon _{ijt} are independent of each other and among themselves.
 
(see: The unbalanced nested error component regression model (B. H. Baltagi et al., 2001)). 

So, can I use INLA to estimate the parameters and components of variance? How can I apply in R-INLA 

Best wishes
Charles
